dudas.texto:
The OoOS policy allows players to batch things that the game rules do not allow to be batched - by the CRD alone, nothing can be batched because that’s not how the game works.

However, to legally batch things under the OoOS exception, the order in which the actions being batched are carried out must make no difference to the resolution of the sequence. In this case, that’s not true, because the order of questing will change the lore value gained - so it cannot be a legally batched sequence.

If the batched action is not legal, then it can’t really be considered a “batched action” for the take back policy, and is instead a game error.

(Although ultimately whether or not to allow a take back here doesn’t actually matter, because there was still a GRE either way so the rewind will do the same thing as a take back would and they would still receive the corrective action whether a take back was allowed or not).

For Chris:
OoOS - Out of Order Sequencing (policy in the tournament rules)
CRD - comprehensive rules document

I've told other players this: never let your opponent decide if you're calling a judge. You can let them know that you're going to call a judge, but it isn't a group decision. It's never "should we call a judge?" Always "I'm calling the judge.".
There have been lots of words written recently about how players are getting away with rules violations. I don't know how true or overblown those are, but if they are accurate, part of the reason is that players don't call judges when they should. Did a player who was caught breaking the rules in round 10 just make a mistake? Or have they been doing it all day and only now her caught? We won't know if they talk their opponents in rounds 1-9 out of calling a judge.

The solutions presented end up becoming harsher consequences for those already trying to follow the rules. In the end, the cheaters get caught and bounced more often than not with current rules (EDIT: Personal Opinion). dudas.texto:
Actions "effects" don't use the bag, that is also what resolves when the action is played.
I don't think "During your turn, when you discard a card, you may play it from your discard." is part of what resolves when the action is played, hence my take on calling this part an "ability", specifically a triggered one, and calling the "Deal 2 damage to chosen character." part of the actions its actual "effect".
5.4.1.2. Actions are played from a player’s hand. When an action is played, its effect resolves immediately. An action is put into the Play zone while the effect resolves. After the effect resolves, the action is put into the player’s discard pile. An effect from an action doesn’t enter the bag. (See 7.7, “Bag.”)

And this also leads to the question of why those 2 parts were not separated by paragraph breaks like they are on Escape Plan or Sing Together Songs and like it's prescribed by :
6.1.1.1. A card can have multiple abilities. These are normally separated by paragraph breaks as well as keywords or story names.

(Also the Sing Together Keyword is defined as an "ability" in :
8.12.1. The Sing Together keyword represents a static ability [...]
And this even though it appears only on Action cards despite what "not an ability" defenders might say about enforcing this :
5.4.3. Effects – Actions have effects rather than abilities
)

dudas.texto: Does this mean if you give Lilo - Bundled up resist with something and it "takes" 0 damage it uses up the ability and it would take damage normally the next instance?
dudas.content_original: > 1.9.5. If a character or effect would deal damage and that damage is reduced to 0 when modifiers are applied, the character or effect is still considered to “deal” damage. If a character or location is dealt damage and that damage is reduced to 0 when modifiers are applied, the character or location “takes” no damage.   > Example: A player has Merida –Formidable Archer in play. Merida has the ability Steady Aim that reads, “Whenever one of your actions deals damage to an opposing character, deal 2 damage to that character.” The player plays Smash, an action that has the effect, “Deal 3 damage to chosen character.” The player chooses Namaari – Resolute Daughter, a character with Resist +3. Smash deals 3 damage,but Namaari takes 0 damage because of Resist +3. Because Smash is still considered to deal damage, Merida’s Steady Aim triggered ability occurs and is added to the bag. Going back to the Temporary Shift topic for a minute, has there been any conversation around how the CRD defines Temporary Shift as having a secondary condition? 8.10.8.5 says “At the end of your turn, if this card is in play, remove all damage…”

I get that Temporary Shift creates a delayed triggered ability. So end of turn happens, marble enters the bag. But we know abilities that have secondary conditions check when you go to resolve them. So we have to check if the card is still in play. 5.1.1.8 thankfully very clearly defines that as “A card that’s faceup in the Play zone with no cards on top of it is considered to be in play.”

My concern is that by following the CRD as currently written, a Temporary shift card that has had another card shifted on top of it would be no longer in play as defined by the CRD, leading to the conclusion that nothing happens with the delayed trigger. But that contradicts the set notes. I guess I’m just wondering if this has been pointed out yet as far as anyone knows. (editado)jueves, 16 de julio de 2026, 20:
